questions.stem: Jainism has 24 TIRTHANKARAS ('ford-makers'). The FIRST Tirthankara was:

options.option_text: RISHABHANATHA (also called ADINATHA) — the founder; mentioned in Rig Veda + Vishnu Purana as a great ascetic

questions.explanation: TIRTHANKARAS of JAINISM — 24 great teachers who crossed the 'ocean of samsara' + helped others across ('tirtha' = ford). (1) RISHABHANATHA / ADINATHA / ADISHWARA — FIRST, founder of Jainism; mentioned in Rig Veda (as Vrishabha) + Bhagavata Purana. Symbol: BULL. (2)-(22) include Ajitnatha, Sambhavanatha, Chandraprabha (moon), Suparshvanatha, Shantinatha, Kunthunatha, Aranatha, Mallinatha (only female in Shvetambara; but male per Digambara), Munisuvrata, Neminatha/Arishtanemi (22nd, cousin of Krishna per Jain tradition). (23) PARSHVANATHA — 23rd, HISTORICAL figure (c. 872-772 BCE); preached 4 vows (ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha); symbol: SNAKE. (24) MAHAVIRA — 24th + LAST (c. 540-468 BCE); added brahmacharya (celibacy) as 5th vow. SYMBOLS (lanchanas) of each Tirthankara are distinct (bull, elephant, lotus, snake, etc.). PANCH MAHAVRATAS (5 great vows): (a) AHIMSA (non-violence); (b) SATYA (truth); (c) ASTEYA (non-stealing); (d) BRAHMACHARYA (celibacy/continence); (e) APARIGRAHA (non-possession / non-attachment). TRIRATNA (3 jewels of Jainism): samyak darshana (right faith), samyak gnyana (right knowledge), samyak charitra (right conduct). Jainism rejects Vedic authority; denies creator God; accepts karma + soul (jiva) but not supreme deity. COSMOLOGY: eternal cycle of utsarpini (ascending) + avasarpini (descending) eras, each with 24 Tirthankaras.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: MAHAVIRA, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, was born in:

options.option_text: KUNDAGRAMA (near Vaishali, modern Bihar) in 540 BCE — to Kshatriya parents Siddhartha + Trishala of the Jnatrika clan

questions.explanation: MAHAVIRA (540-468 BCE per traditional dating; some give 599-527 BCE) — 24th + last Tirthankara of Jainism. BIRTH: KUNDAGRAMA / KSHATRIYAKUND — a suburb of VAISHALI (modern Basokund, Muzaffarpur district, BIHAR). PARENTS: King SIDDHARTHA (of the Jnatrika / Jnatrika Kshatriya clan) + Queen TRISHALA (sister of Chetaka, king of Vaishali; so Mahavira was a prince by birth). Chetaka's daughter Chellana married Bimbisara of Magadha → Mahavira + Buddha's royal circles overlapped. ORIGINAL NAME: VARDHAMANA (meaning 'prosperity-increasing'). Married YASHODA, had a daughter PRIYADARSHANA. At AGE 30, after parents' death, renounced the world; wandered 12 YEARS as an ascetic. KAIVALYA (omniscient enlightenment) attained at 42 at JRIMBHIKAGRAMA (near Rijupalika River) under a SAL TREE. Given title 'MAHAVIRA' ('great hero') + 'JINA' ('conqueror of passions') — hence JAINISM. Preached for 30 years; attained NIRVANA / MOKSHA at age 72 at PAVAPURI (modern Pawapuri, Nalanda district, Bihar — where Jalmandir stands today) in 468 BCE (per traditional). TITLES: Mahavira, Jina, Arihanta, Nirgrantha (bondless), Kevalin. MAIN DISCIPLES: 11 GANADHARAS (chief disciples) — INDRABHUTI GAUTAMA was the chief; SUDHARMAN / SUDHARMA was the last surviving, whose successor JAMBU was the last Jain to attain Kevala Jnana in our age. CONTEMPORARY of BUDDHA (566/480 BCE). Both in BIHAR, both from Kshatriya royal families, both rejected Vedic ritual + caste hierarchy.

questions.stem: The FIVE GREAT VOWS (Panch Mahavratas) of Jainism include ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha + a fifth added by Mahavira:

options.option_text: BRAHMACHARYA — celibacy/continence; added by Mahavira to Parshvanatha's original 4 vows

questions.explanation: PANCH MAHAVRATAS ('5 great vows') of JAINISM (for monks + nuns; laypeople observe lighter 'anuvratas'): (1) AHIMSA — NON-VIOLENCE in thought, word + deed. Core of Jainism — extends to NOT harming any life form including microbes. Jain monks sweep the path ahead with soft brush (rajoharana), strain water, wear face masks (muhpatti) to avoid inhaling insects. (2) SATYA — truthfulness. (3) ASTEYA — non-stealing; not taking anything not freely given. (4) APARIGRAHA — non-possession / non-attachment; some Jain monks (Digambara) renounce even clothes. (5) BRAHMACHARYA — celibacy/continence. ADDED by MAHAVIRA to Parshvanatha's ORIGINAL FOUR vows (chauryam: the 5th was not codified earlier). PARSHVANATHA (23rd Tirthankara, c. 872-772 BCE) was a HISTORICAL figure, 250 years before Mahavira; his original chaturyama included four vows; Mahavira added the 5th to strengthen sexual discipline. JAINISM PHILOSOPHY: (a) KARMA theory — much more atomistic/particulate than Hindu view; karmic particles stick to soul; ascetic practice burns them off (nirjara) + prevents new influx (samvara) + leads to moksha. (b) ANEKANTAVADA — 'doctrine of many-sidedness' / non-absolutism; reality has multiple aspects; no single view is complete. (c) SYADVADA — 'doctrine of may-be' / 7-fold predication; every statement qualified with 'syat' ('perhaps'). (d) NAYAVADA — theory of standpoints. Jainism champions PLURALISM + epistemological humility. ALL life has SOUL (jiva) — organised in 5 categories by senses (1-sense microbes to 5-sense humans); 3 worlds of samsara.

questions.stem: After Mahavira's death (468 BCE), Jainism SPLIT into two major sects. They are:

options.option_text: DIGAMBARA (sky-clad/nude monks) + SHVETAMBARA (white-clad monks) — split around 1st c. BCE / CE over migration to south + monastic robes

questions.explanation: JAIN SCHISM — SECTS formed ~1st c. BCE / CE: (1) DIGAMBARA ('sky-clad' / nude) — monks go naked; believe COMPLETE renunciation requires shedding of ALL possessions including clothes. Hold that: (a) WOMEN CANNOT achieve moksha (must be reborn as man first); (b) 19th Tirthankara MALLI was MALE (not female as Shvetambara holds); (c) Mahavira did not marry (vs Shvetambara view that he did); (d) A kevalin does not need food. Dominant in KARNATAKA + parts of MP/Rajasthan. Key figures: Kundakunda, Umaswami (author of Tattvartha Sutra). (2) SHVETAMBARA ('white-clad') — monks + nuns wear simple WHITE ROBES + keep minimum possessions (bowl, brush, muhpatti). Allow WOMEN's ordination + liberation. Dominant in GUJARAT + Rajasthan. Main canonical scriptures: AGAMAS (~45 texts). CAUSE of SCHISM: great FAMINE in Magadha (~298 BCE) during Chandragupta Maurya's reign. Jain leader BHADRABAHU migrated with a group of monks SOUTH to Sravanabelagola (Karnataka); STHULABHADRA stayed in Magadha + held First Jain Council there. When Bhadrabahu's group returned, they found the Magadha Jains had relaxed some rules (adopting white robes) — conflict widened over centuries + formalised into Digambara (southern group) vs Shvetambara (Magadha/later migration). LATER sub-sects: Shvetambara → Murtipujaka (idol-worshippers) + Sthanakvasi (non-idolatrous, 17th c. Lonka Shah) + Terapanthi. Digambara → Bisapanthi, Terapanthi (Dig), Taranpanthi (no idols). NOTE: Digambara-Terapanthi + Shvetambara-Terapanthi are DIFFERENT.

questions.stem: The FIRST JAIN COUNCIL (Prathama Samiti) was held around 300 BCE at:

options.option_text: PATALIPUTRA — presided by STHULABHADRA during Chandragupta Maurya's reign; compiled 12 Angas of canonical literature

questions.explanation: JAIN COUNCILS — two major canonical councils. (1) FIRST JAIN COUNCIL (Prathama Samiti) — held ~300 BCE at PATALIPUTRA under the presidency of STHULABHADRA during the reign of CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA. CONTEXT: great Magadha famine prompted BHADRABAHU to migrate south with half of the sangha to Sravanabelagola (modern Karnataka). The monks who remained in Magadha convened the council to compile the canon — compiled 12 ANGAS (canonical texts) but the 12th (Drishtivada) was already lost, so only 11 were preserved. The returning Digambara faction rejected this compilation (saying it was incomplete + corrupted). This ASSEMBLY'S failure to be universally accepted was the SEED of the Digambara-Shvetambara schism. (2) SECOND JAIN COUNCIL — held at VALABHI (Gujarat) ~5th-6th c. CE (453 or 466 CE) under DEVARDDHI KSHAMASHRAMANA. Final RE-compilation of Jain canon — 45 AGAMAS (canonical texts) of Shvetambara tradition committed to writing for the first time (till then oral). Digambara tradition holds that original Mahavira teachings were LOST in toto; no canonical agreement with Shvetambara. NOTABLE JAIN LITERATURE: (a) KALPA SUTRA (by Bhadrabahu, lives of Tirthankaras); (b) TATTVARTHA SUTRA (by Umaswami, ~2nd c. CE, common to both sects); (c) PRAKRIT language used for most early Jain texts (Ardhamagadhi dialect); (d) later Sanskrit + regional languages. JAINISM FLOURISHED in KARNATAKA, GUJARAT, RAJASTHAN, MAHARASHTRA + TAMIL NADU (Sangam era). Royal patrons: Chandragupta Maurya (convert in old age per tradition), Kharavela of Kalinga (Hathigumpha inscription 150 BCE), Amoghavarsha (Rashtrakuta), Kumarapala (Chalukya Gujarat), Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagar. Famous Jain temples: Mount Abu (Dilwara), Shravanabelagola (Gommateshwara statue), Palitana (Gujarat — 863 temples on Shatrunjaya hill), Ranakpur, Khajuraho (Parshvanatha temple).

questions.stem: The MONOLITHIC STATUE OF BAHUBALI (Gommateshwara), 57-ft tall, at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka was erected by:

options.option_text: CHAMUNDARAYA — minister of the Ganga king Rachamalla IV, in 981 CE; world's largest monolithic statue at the time

questions.explanation: GOMMATESHWARA / BAHUBALI MONOLITH at SHRAVANABELAGOLA (Hassan district, KARNATAKA) — a 57-FOOT (17.4m) tall single-stone GRANITE statue of BAHUBALI (a son of Rishabhanatha, first Tirthankara). ERECTED: 981 CE by CHAMUNDARAYA, the Jain minister + commander of Ganga king Rachamalla IV (Western Ganga dynasty). Sculptor: Aristanemi. At the time, one of the world's largest monolithic sculptures. Stands atop VINDHYAGIRI HILL; Chandragiri hill nearby is believed to be the site where Emperor CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA ended his life by sallekhana (fasting to death) in his final years as a Jain monk under Acharya Bhadrabahu. MAHAMASTAKABHISHEKA — the grand head-anointing ceremony held every 12 YEARS — milk, saffron, ghee, sugarcane juice, sandal paste + 10008 kalashas of water poured over the statue from scaffolding; attracts millions of pilgrims + tourists. 12-year interval ceremonies: 2006, 2018, next in 2030. KARNATAKA STATE HERITAGE list's jewel; candidate for UNESCO World Heritage. OTHER major JAIN HERITAGE: (1) DILWARA TEMPLES, Mount Abu (Rajasthan) — 11th-13th c., marble work among the finest in world; 5 main temples incl. Vimal Vasahi (for Adinath), Luna Vasahi (for Neminath). (2) RANAKPUR Chaturmukha temple (Rajasthan) — 1444 pillars, no two alike; one of largest + busiest Jain temples. (3) SHIKHAR JI / PARASNATH HILL (Jharkhand) — 20 of 24 Tirthankaras attained moksha here; holiest Jain pilgrimage. (4) PALITANA (Shatrunjaya Hill, Gujarat) — 863 Jain temples; Shvetambara holy site. (5) KHAJURAHO (MP) — Jain temple group (Parshvanatha etc.) along with Hindu temples (UNESCO since 1986). (6) UDAYAGIRI + KHANDAGIRI caves (Odisha) — from Kharavela's era (c. 150 BCE); Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela = only Jain royal inscription of magnitude.

questions.stem: KHARAVELA, the great Jain king of KALINGA, is known for which famous inscription?

options.option_text: HATHIGUMPHA INSCRIPTION — carved in Udayagiri Caves near Bhubaneswar (~150 BCE); earliest known biographical rock edict of a Jain king

questions.explanation: KHARAVELA (c. 193-170 BCE, approx) — great Jain king of KALINGA (modern Odisha), 3rd ruler of CHEDI / MAHAMEGHAVAHANA dynasty. Ascended throne at 24. HATHIGUMPHA ('Elephant Cave') INSCRIPTION — at UDAYAGIRI + KHANDAGIRI twin-hill Jain caves near Bhubaneswar (Odisha), dated ~150 BCE. The inscription is in PRAKRIT + BRAHMI script; 17 lines; records Kharavela's achievements in chronological order year-wise (first such autobiography-like record in India). CONTENTS: (1) Kharavela's education + early career. (2) 5th year — extended Tansulya Canal (dug by a Nanda king) — CHATTEENMETE (400 km canal). (3) 8th year — attacked Rajagriha (Magadha). (4) 12th year — humbled Magadhan king + extended empire; brought back the Jain IDOL (carried away by Nandas earlier) — SIGNIFICANT as Kalinga was recovering spiritual icons. (5) 13th year — renovation of JAIN CAVES on Kumari Hill (Udayagiri-Khandagiri). (6) Built temples, aqueducts, pleasure-parks. FOUND (rediscovered) by British archaeologist ALEXANDER CUNNINGHAM + Lt. Markham Kittoe in 1837; deciphered by James Prinsep (who decoded Brahmi ~1837). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) only extensive Jain royal inscription from early India; (2) shows Jainism's vigor in Odisha in 2nd c. BCE; (3) provides historical picture of post-Ashokan period — Kharavela defeated Demetrius (Yavana = Indo-Greek) in Mathura (per some readings); (4) mentions BRIHADRATHAS, MAGADHAS, musicians + poets; (5) mentions recovery of the Kalinga-Jina from Nanda-period spoliation. UDAYAGIRI + KHANDAGIRI caves — 18 + 15 caves respectively; rock-cut residential + meditational chambers for Jain monks; famous caves include RANI GUMPHA (Queen's cave, two-storeyed, sculpted reliefs), GANESHA GUMPHA, HATHIGUMPHA. Protected monuments; major tourist site. Kharavela ranks alongside Ashoka + Samudragupta as one of ancient India's greatest empire-builders of Indian east.

questions.stem: SALLEKHANA / SANTHARA in Jainism refers to:

options.option_text: RITUAL FASTING to death — voluntary, gradual cessation of food + water near end of life; seen as spiritual culmination, NOT suicide

questions.explanation: SALLEKHANA (also called SANTHARA / SAMADHI MARANA) — ritual practice in Jainism of voluntary, gradual CESSATION of food + water as one nears death (old age, incurable illness, or facing unavoidable death). Seen as the SPIRITUAL CULMINATION of a Jain life — dying with equanimity, without fear, freeing soul from bodily attachments, burning off remaining karma. Performed with guidance of a Jain monk + family. TAKES weeks / months of gradual reduction (rather than abrupt). Distinguished from suicide (which is rejected in Jainism as karmic bondage) — sallekhana is: (a) gradual, not abrupt; (b) chosen when death is INEVITABLE anyway; (c) performed with awareness + detachment; (d) not from passion/despair. HISTORICAL: CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA is believed to have practiced sallekhana at CHANDRAGIRI hill, Shravanabelagola, under BHADRABAHU's guidance (c. 298 BCE); his inscription there (Bhadrabahu cave). About 200-300 Jains still practice sallekhana annually in India (mostly Digambara + Shvetambara Terapanthi). LEGAL CONTROVERSY: (1) 2015 — RAJASTHAN HC in Nikhil Soni v. UoI ruled sallekhana was SUICIDE under IPC 306/309 + banned the practice. (2) Major Jain community protests; rallies in Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur. (3) SUPREME COURT STAYED the Rajasthan HC ruling (31 Aug 2015) recognising sallekhana as a legitimate religious practice under Article 25 (freedom of religion). CASE STILL PENDING. (4) Compare with KARUNA MERCY KILLING / ACTIVE EUTHANASIA debate (Aruna Shanbaug case 2011 + 2018 Common Cause v. UOI — passive euthanasia + living wills ALLOWED). Sallekhana falls between suicide + euthanasia, occupying a unique religious-cultural-legal space. ALMOST all world faiths have analogues: Hindu sanyasin's renunciation unto death, Buddhist self-starvation (rare), Vaishnavite Samadhi. KEY to Jainism's emphasis on ahimsa — self-directed non-violence + peaceful exit.

questions.stem: CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA, founder of the Mauryan Empire, is said to have become a JAIN monk in his final years + died by sallekhana at:

options.option_text: SHRAVANABELAGOLA (Chandragiri Hill) in Karnataka — under the guidance of Jain acharya BHADRABAHU, around 298 BCE

questions.explanation: CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA (c. 340-298 BCE) — founder of MAURYAN EMPIRE (322 BCE); mentored by CHANAKYA/KAUTILYA (author of Arthashastra); overthrew Nanda dynasty; built India's first subcontinental empire (Hindu Kush to Bengal, Himalayas to Deccan); defeated SELEUCUS NICATOR (Alexander's successor) in 305 BCE, gained Afghanistan + married his daughter Helen; received Seleucus's ambassador MEGASTHENES (author of 'Indika'). JAIN CONVERSION: per Jain tradition (Digambara), Chandragupta abdicated the throne ~298 BCE (after a 24-year reign), became disciple of JAIN ACHARYA BHADRABAHU, + migrated SOUTH with him when a great famine struck Magadha. Lived final years at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka) + died by SALLEKHANA (ritual fast to death) at CHANDRAGIRI HILL. Chandragiri inscription (attributed to later period but references BHADRABAHU's cave) supports this. Succeeded by son BINDUSARA. HISTORICAL DEBATE: not all scholars accept the Jain tradition; some (like V.A. Smith) held it legendary. But (a) the Sravanabelagola tradition is ancient + consistent; (b) cave named for Bhadrabahu at Chandragiri; (c) Chandragupta's name inscribed in later record. BROADLY ACCEPTED as historically plausible. SIGNIFICANCE: (1) shows Jainism's appeal to royal elite in 4th c. BCE; (2) indicates Jain presence in south India TWO centuries before Ashoka's missions; (3) bridges Magadha + Deccan Jainism historically. OTHER royal Jain patrons: BIMBISARA (Magadha), AJATASHATRU (Magadha, met Mahavira), CHANDANA (first female disciple of Mahavira, daughter of King Dadhivahana of Champa), SUPRATIBUDDHA, KHARAVELA (Kalinga), KUMARAPALA (Chalukya, 12th c.), AMOGHAVARSHA (Rashtrakuta, 9th c. — patronised Jinasena + Gunabhadra; author of 'Kavirajamarga' in Kannada; abdicated himself in Jain style). JAIN POPULATION TODAY: ~0.4% of Indian population (~45 lakh), but DISPROPORTIONATELY affluent + influential in trade + philanthropy + minoritystatus (2014).

questions.stem: The TRIRATNA (three jewels) of Jainism for attaining moksha are:

options.option_text: SAMYAK DARSHAN (right faith), SAMYAK GNYANA (right knowledge), SAMYAK CHARITRA (right conduct)

questions.explanation: TRIRATNA ('three jewels') or RATNATRAYA of JAINISM — the path to MOKSHA (liberation from samsara): (1) SAMYAK DARSHANA — 'right faith' / right vision / right perception; seeing reality as it is (through the 9 tattvas — soul, non-soul, asrava, bandha, samvara, nirjara, moksha, punya, papa); belief in Tirthankaras + their teachings. (2) SAMYAK GNYANA — 'right knowledge' / scriptural + experiential comprehension; understanding through anekantavada (multi-perspectival). (3) SAMYAK CHARITRA — 'right conduct' / ethical practice; following the 5 mahavratas + the 5 samitis (carefulness) + 3 guptis (restraint) + 10 dharmas + 12 reflections (bhavanas). All 3 together → moksha; one alone insufficient. JAIN COSMOLOGY: the universe is ETERNAL (no creator God); has 6 eternal substances (dravyas) — soul (jiva), matter (pudgala), motion principle (dharma), rest principle (adharma), space (akasha), time (kala). Souls are INFINITE in number, each potentially capable of liberation. LOKA (universe) is shaped like a STANDING HUMAN — Urdhvaloka (upper), Madhyaloka (middle — where we are), Adholoka (lower hells). 14 gunasthanas (stages of spiritual progress). JAIN CALENDAR: Vira Nirvana Samvat starts 527 BCE from Mahavira's nirvana — currently VS 2552. PARYUSHANA — 8-day holiest Jain festival (Aug-Sep); fasting, prayer, CONFESSION of faults; ends with KSHAMAVANI (forgiveness day) — 'Michhami Dukkadam' (asking/giving forgiveness). MAHAVIR JAYANTI — 13th day of Chaitra Shukla paksha; public holiday in India. JAIN FESTIVALS: Diwali (Mahavira's nirvana day!), Bhogali Purnima, Akshaya Tritiya (Rishabhanatha's end of year-long fast).
